theme: Everyone guesses, one must be right
title: Everyone Guesses, One Must Be Right
seed_problem: hat-guessing configuration: solver outputs a deterministic strategy table, scored against all adversarial colour assignments
mutation: composite: full guess-table output (a general covering code, not just a residue trick) coupled to per-player information weights and worst-case-over-all-assignments scoring, so the strategy designer must both (a) discover that only a pre-agreed covering code guarantees any worst-case correctness at all and (b) balance WHICH players anchor which residue class by their information weight -- turning a classic puzzle fact into a weighted load-balancing optimization under adversarial evaluation.
strategies: trivial: index round-robin residue assignment, ignoring weights entirely (reproduces the checker baseline)
naive greedy: balance residues one player at a time in the given input order (no lookahead, no re-sorting) -- light groups get committed to filler weight before the big, informative players arrive

insight (strong): sort players by weight descending first, then greedily balance (classic LPT / exchange-argument load balancing), placing the most informative guessers while every residue group is still empty
a general solver can go further still: abandon the linear "assumed total mod K" family entirely and design a genuinely non-linear covering code tailored to the exact weight profile
